the minor groove of Gua in the recognition sequence plays a crucial role for restriction enzymes BglII and BamHI, whereas it does not affect the recognition process of EcoRI.

the 2-amino groups of Gua and Ade are not indispensable for the recognition of the enzymes BglII and BamHI, but for EcoRI.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exocyclic amino group of Gua plays a significant role in the recognition of restriction endoncleases to DNA.
the minor groove of Gua plays important roles in the molecular recognition of BglII, and EcoRI and BamHIs.
the minor groove of Gua is not essential for the cleavage efficiency of the restriction enzymes BglII, BamHI and EcoRI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BglII, a type II restriction endonucase, can be used as a model system for the study of the influence of the minor groove on biomolecular interactions.
BglII and/or EcoRI can be employed for the cleavage of DNA with hypoxanthine (in place of adenine) at 37 degrees C.
the molecular influence of Hyp on DNA cleavage efficiencies of BglII, BamHI and EcoRI is dependent on the DNA sequences of recognition sites.
